title: ALM examines alternative investment models in Big Law
summary: ALM reports on growing interest in minority investment structures for law firms in the U.S. and U.K., as traditional private equity approaches face structural challenges in partnership-based firms. Chief Development Officer Travis Lenkner describes a model centered on long-term capital, where investors participate through profit distributions, aligning more closely with law firm economics and governance.
body_markdown:
ALM reports on growing interest in minority investment structures for law firms in the U.S. and U.K., as traditional private equity approaches face structural challenges in partnership-based firms. Chief Development Officer[Travis Lenkner](https://www.burfordcapital.com/about-us/our-team/travis-lenkner/) describes a model centered on long-term capital, where investors participate through profit distributions, aligning more closely with law firm economics and governance.


Read the full article[here](https://www.law.com/international-edition/2026/04/02/burford-capital-the-traditional-private-equity-playbook-will-not-work-in-big-law/) .
